foods.name: pumpkin
foods.answer: Yes, at a normal serve. Monash lists 75 g of kabocha (Japanese or Kent) pumpkin as low. Reported lab data puts it at moderate from 162 g and high from 206 g, from fructans. Canned pumpkin is low at 75 g (⅓ cup). Other squashes, such as butternut, have smaller low serves.

servings.note: The 75 g serve is on Monash's public shopping list. The moderate and high amounts are as reported by dietitian sites from Monash data.
Grams as reported by dietitian sites from Monash data. The pumpkin variety inside the can isn't stated.

changes.text: Kabocha first tested with no FODMAPs at all. A later Monash retest found fructans in bigger portions, so it now has a 75 g low serve.

disagreements.text: FODMAP Friendly's lab reportedly rates Japanese or Kent pumpkin lower: 57 g raw, or 75 g cooked with a 94 g maximum.
For canned pumpkin, FODMAP Friendly reportedly allows 120 g, up to 150 g, and found GOS as well as fructans.

notes.text: Monash lists Japanese pumpkin among its low FODMAP swaps in its Step 1 guide.
In Monash's roasted pepper and pumpkin dip, using butternut instead of Japanese pumpkin means splitting the batch into more servings to stay within limits.

faq.q: Is butternut squash low FODMAP like pumpkin?
faq.a: Only in a smaller portion. Dietitian sites report Monash's low serve for unpeeled butternut at 63 g, below kabocha's 75 g.

faq.q: Is pumpkin pie low FODMAP?
faq.a: The filling can fit if each slice holds no more than about 75 g of canned pumpkin. The crust, milk and sweetener need checking too.

foods.name: arugula
foods.answer: Yes. Monash's standard serve of arugula (rocket) is 1 cup, about 35 g, and it reportedly found only trace FODMAPs. Dietitian sites say it stayed low up to 500 g, the largest amount tested, so it works as a salad base.

servings.note: Only trace FODMAPs were found, so this is a normal portion, not a limit. The source names no FODMAP group.

changes.text: For years Monash reported no FODMAPs in arugula. An app update changed this to trace amounts, still with no upper limit.

disagreements.text: Karlijn's Kitchen gives the largest still-low amount instead of a standard serve: up to 500 g.

faq.q: Is arugula pesto low FODMAP?
faq.a: The arugula is fine. Most pesto recipes add garlic, so use garlic-infused oil in its place.

foods.name: bok choy
foods.answer: Yes, at a standard serve. Monash lists 75 g of bok choy, about 1 cup chopped, as low. Dietitian sites report a moderate amount of sorbitol from 100 g, so a very large stir-fry portion can tip it over.

servings.note: The moderate amount is as reported by Karlijn's Kitchen from Monash data.

notes.text: Monash's Step 1 guide and its public food list both name bok choy as a low FODMAP vegetable.

faq.q: Can I have bok choy in a stir-fry every day?
faq.a: Yes, if each meal stays near 75 g. Bigger amounts add sorbitol, which adds up with other polyol foods in the same meal.

foods.name: leek
foods.answer: Partly. The dark green leaves are low: Monash's serve is 1 cup chopped (75 g), and they reportedly stayed low up to 500 g. The white bulb holds fructans, so only about 14 g of it (2 generous tablespoons, finely chopped) is reported as low.

servings.note: Reported to stay low up to 500 g, the most Monash tested.
No moderate or high amount has been published for the bulb.

changes.text: Monash's leaf serve was first listed as 100 g, then 75 g. A small low serve for the white bulb (14 g) was added later, and an unclear mixed leaf-and-bulb entry was removed.

disagreements.text: Monash's public diet sheets still list leek among high-FODMAP vegetables without saying which part, which fits the bulb rather than the leaves.
FODMAP Friendly's lab reportedly rates ½ cup (37 g) of leaves as low with an 82 g maximum, and 47 g of bulb as low.

notes.text: Monash now uses raw leek bulb as one of its fructan test foods in the reintroduction phase.
Older lab data measured about 0.5 g of fructans per 100 g of whole leek, far less than onion at about 1.8 g.

faq.q: Is leek and potato soup low FODMAP?
faq.a: Only when it's made with the green leaves. Fructans from the white bulb dissolve into the soup, so a classic version is likely high.

foods.name: onion
foods.answer: No. Monash lists onion as high in fructans. Only tiny amounts test low: about 10 g of red onion is the reported Monash low serve, and FODMAP Friendly reportedly rates brown onion high from 30 g. Drained large pickled onions are a lower-FODMAP option.

servings.note: Monash has published no low serve for these onions. The 30 g high point is FODMAP Friendly's, as reported by a dietitian site.
Reported Monash low serve. No moderate or high amount has been published.
Reported to be high in fructans above 107 g. Small pickled onions tested very differently.

changes.text: Monash's low serve for large pickled onions was first 45 g and was later raised to 60 g.

disagreements.text: FODMAP Friendly's lab reportedly allows 26 g of brown onion and 27 g of red onion, more than Monash's 10 g of red onion.
George Eats reports large pickled onions as low up to 84 g, with moderate fructans from 85 g.

notes.text: Older lab data measured about 1.8 g of fructans per 100 g of white onion.
Monash keeps onion of any variety as its test food for onion fructans in the reintroduction phase.
Fructans dissolve in water but not in oil, so onion-infused oil keeps the flavor without the fructans.

faq.q: Does cooking onion make it low FODMAP?
faq.a: Not in normal cooking: fructans move into the water of soups and sauces. Monash found microwaving diced onion in water cut its FODMAPs by 71%, but it still wasn't low.

faq.q: Is onion-infused oil low FODMAP?
faq.a: Yes, as long as the onion pieces are taken out. The fructans stay in the onion, not the oil.

foods.name: spring onion
foods.answer: The green tops, yes. Monash reports ¾ cup (75 g) of spring onion greens as low, with a moderate amount of fructose from 97 g. The white bulb carries fructans: a 32 g Monash low serve is reported, but many guides still say to skip the bulb at first.

servings.note: Grams as reported by dietitian sites from Monash's latest retest.
Reported Monash low serve. No moderate or high amount has been published.

changes.text: Early tests found no FODMAPs in 16 g of greens. A September 2022 retest set 75 g as low and moderate from 265 g. A later retest kept 75 g but moved the moderate point down to 97 g.

disagreements.text: FODMAP Friendly lists the spring onion bulb as high. Its lab reportedly rates scallion greens low at 16 g, with a 160 g maximum.
One George Eats recipe says Monash regards the greens as having negligible FODMAPs, which doesn't match the 97 g moderate point above.

notes.text: Monash suggests the green tops as a garnish for onion flavor without the fructans.
Older lab data found the spring onion bulb rich in fructans, at about 6.3 g per 100 g.

faq.q: Are scallions and spring onions the same thing?
faq.a: Monash lists them as one food. In the US, spring onions can be a variety with a larger bulb, so sticking to the green parts is the simplest rule.

foods.name: shallots
foods.answer: No. Shallots are among the richest sources of fructans, at about 8.9 g per 100 g in lab tests, roughly five times as much as onion. Monash reportedly tested large amounts and found no low serve. Spring onion greens, chives or garlic-infused oil give a similar savory note.

servings.note: No low serve has been published by Monash, and no gram amount for the high point is public.

disagreements.text: FODMAP Friendly's lab reportedly rates 1 g of shallot as low, an amount too small to matter in most cooking.

notes.text: Lab data put shallots at about 8.9 g of fructans per 100 g, behind only garlic and Jerusalem artichoke among the vegetables measured.
Monash names shallots among the main high-FODMAP ingredients in East and South East Asian cooking, including fried shallots and curry pastes.

faq.q: Are fried shallots low FODMAP?
faq.a: No test of fried shallots has been published. Fructans don't move into the frying oil, so they stay in the crispy shallot.

foods.name: fennel
foods.answer: Yes, at a normal serve. Monash's retested low serve is ¾ cup (75 g) of raw fennel bulb. Reported lab data shows a moderate amount of fructose from 145 g and high from 195 g, when fructans appear too. The feathery fronds are low at 3 tablespoons (15 g).

servings.note: Grams as reported by dietitian sites from Monash's retest.

changes.text: Monash's first low serve for raw fennel bulb was ½ cup (49 g). A retest raised it to ¾ cup (75 g).

disagreements.text: George Eats gives the largest still-low amount instead: up to 144 g of bulb, as of August 2026.
FODMAP Friendly reportedly rates ½ cup (48 g) of bulb as low with a 144 g maximum, and names fructans and mannitol.

notes.text: Fennel seeds were reported low at 1 teaspoon (2 g) by both Monash and FODMAP Friendly.

faq.q: Is roasted fennel low FODMAP?
faq.a: The tests used raw bulb, so weigh it before cooking and keep to about 75 g per person.

foods.name: bell pepper
foods.answer: Green bell pepper, yes: Monash lists 75 g as low, with fructans only moderate from 250 g. Red is a different story: about 43 g (⅓ cup) is low, with fructose moderate from 57 g and high from 75 g. Yellow and orange peppers sit close to red.

servings.note: The 75 g serve is on Monash's public shopping list. The moderate and high amounts are as reported by dietitian sites.
Grams as reported by dietitian sites from Monash's retest.

changes.text: Monash first found no FODMAPs in red bell pepper, and its January 2021 fibre guide still listed 75 g as a low serve. A retest cut the low serve to 43 g.
Green bell pepper's low serve went from 52 g in early testing to 75 g after a retest.

disagreements.text: FODMAP Friendly's lab reportedly rates 75 g of red pepper as low, with a maximum of 750 g, later 825 g. For yellow pepper it later found no low amount.
Karlijn's Kitchen gives yellow and orange together as 38 g low, 51 g moderate and 75 g high.

notes.text: Monash's diet sheets list red bell pepper among high-FODMAP vegetables and green bell pepper as the low swap.

faq.q: Are roasted red peppers low FODMAP?
faq.a: We haven't found a public test of roasted peppers. Keep to about 43 g of red pepper per serve, or mix in green pepper for volume.

foods.name: zucchini
foods.answer: Yes, in a modest serve. Monash's current diet sheet lists 65 g of zucchini as low. Reported lab data shows moderate fructans from 75 g and high from 87 g, so one medium zucchini, about 195 g, is more than a single low serve.

servings.note: The 65 g serve is from Monash's 2026 diet sheet. The moderate and high amounts are as reported by dietitian sites.

disagreements.text: George Eats reports zucchini as low up to 74 g as of August 2026, with moderate fructans from 75 g. An earlier report put the low serve at 67 g.
FODMAP Friendly's lab reportedly rates 75 g of raw green zucchini as low, with a 525 g maximum.

notes.text: Monash weighs one medium zucchini at about 195 g in its recipes.

faq.q: Is zucchini bread low FODMAP?
faq.a: It depends more on the flour and sweetener. Spread across a whole loaf, the zucchini in one slice is usually a small amount.

foods.name: edamame
foods.answer: Yes, at a normal serve. Dietitian sites report a Monash low serve of 75 g of shelled edamame, and the newest report says it stays low up to about 195 g before fructans turn moderate. Edamame behaves very differently from mature soybeans, which are high FODMAP.

servings.note: Grams as reported by dietitian sites from Monash data. See below for the larger still-low amount.

changes.text: Earlier reports gave ½ cup (90 g, cooked) as the low serve, with high fructans from 210 g.

disagreements.text: George Eats reports edamame as low up to 195 g as of August 2026, with moderate fructans in larger serves.

notes.text: Mature soybeans are high in GOS and fructans, so whole soybeans and milk made from them are not the same as edamame.

faq.q: Does edamame have GOS like other beans?
faq.a: Reported testing names fructans, not GOS, as the FODMAP that builds up in large edamame servings.

foods.name: jalapeño
foods.answer: Yes, in normal amounts. Dietitian sites report a Monash low serve of 30 g of raw jalapeño (one small chile), with fructose moderate from about 40 g. Pickled jalapeños had only trace FODMAPs and stayed low up to 500 g, the most tested.

servings.note: Grams as reported by dietitian sites from Monash data.
Only trace FODMAPs were found, and it stayed low up to 500 g, so this is a normal portion, not a limit.

disagreements.text: George Eats gives the largest still-low amount for raw jalapeño instead: up to 39 g.

notes.text: Peppers contain capsaicin, which can cause heartburn or stomach pain in some people for reasons unrelated to FODMAPs.

faq.q: Is salsa with jalapeño low FODMAP?
faq.a: The jalapeño is fine in small amounts, but most store-bought salsa also has onion and garlic, so read the label.

foods.name: sauerkraut
foods.answer: Only a small spoonful. Fermenting cabbage turns some of its sugar into mannitol, a polyol. Monash rates 1 tablespoon as low and a full cup as high. Dietitian sites report 2 tablespoons (23 g) as low, with a moderate amount of mannitol from 35 g.

servings.note: Grams as reported by Karlijn's Kitchen. Monash says a full cup is high but gives no gram figure for it.

changes.text: Monash now uses white-cabbage sauerkraut as one of its mannitol test foods in the reintroduction phase.

disagreements.text: Monash's 2016 post put the low serve at 1 tablespoon, smaller than the 2 tablespoons (23 g) that dietitian sites now report.

notes.text: Plain cabbage is low in a 1 cup serve, but the same cup fermented into sauerkraut is high in mannitol.
Red cabbage sauerkraut rated moderate in Monash's table, against high for the white version. A dietitian site reported it low at ½ cup in older app data.

faq.q: Can I eat sauerkraut for gut health on a low FODMAP diet?
faq.a: A spoonful fits. Larger servings add mannitol, so try them during the reintroduction phase instead.

foods.name: kimchi
foods.answer: In a small side portion. Dietitian sites report that Monash lists 47 g of kimchi as low, with a moderate amount of mannitol from 71 g. As with sauerkraut, fermentation creates mannitol. Recipes and brands vary, so the tested kimchi may not match yours.

servings.note: Grams as reported by Karlijn's Kitchen from the Monash app.

changes.text: In 2016 a dietitian site noted Monash hadn't tested kimchi yet. By 2024 a tested serve of 47 g was being reported.

notes.text: Lactic fermentation converts fructose in cabbage into mannitol, which is why fermented cabbage tests higher than fresh.

faq.q: Is kimchi high FODMAP?
faq.a: Not in a side-dish portion of about 47 g. A big bowl adds mannitol, so keep it as a topping or side.

foods.name: ginger
foods.answer: Yes. Monash's low serve for fresh ginger is 5 g, raised from 3 g, with no upper limit given, and FODMAP Friendly reportedly found no FODMAPs at all. Fresh ginger is a handy way to add flavor in place of onion and garlic.

servings.note: No upper limit was given. The source names no FODMAP group.

changes.text: Monash's serve for fresh ginger was first 1 teaspoon (3 g) and was raised to 5 g after more testing.

disagreements.text: FODMAP Friendly reportedly found no FODMAPs in fresh ginger or in plain pickled ginger.

notes.text: Monash names ginger, with garlic-infused oil and spring onion greens, as a versatile flavor base for low FODMAP cooking.
Ginger ale is reported low up to 244 g in Monash data. No Monash entry for ground ginger was found.

faq.q: Is ginger tea low FODMAP?
faq.a: Ginger tea itself hasn't been tested, but a homemade infusion of fresh ginger is likely fine given ginger's results.

faq.q: Is ground ginger low FODMAP?
faq.a: No public test was found. It's likely similar to fresh ginger, but that's an assumption, not a lab result.

foods.name: cinnamon
foods.answer: Probably fine in normal amounts. Monash names cinnamon among spices used in low FODMAP cooking, and a dietitian site reports a Monash-tested serve of 1 teaspoon. We found no public gram figure, so we can't show a lab-tested amount here.

estimateAnswer.line: A 1 teaspoon serve is reported to have passed Monash testing, but no gram figure is public.

servings.note: No public gram figure, so no amounts are shown. The source names no FODMAP group.

notes.text: Monash lists cinnamon in its Mexican cuisine row and other cuisine rows of low FODMAP herbs and spices.
Monash advises avoiding seasoning mixes and blends, which can hide garlic or onion.

faq.q: Can I bake with cinnamon on a low FODMAP diet?
faq.a: Yes. A teaspoon spread through a recipe is a small amount per serve; the flour and sweetener matter far more.

foods.name: cilantro
foods.answer: Yes. Fresh cilantro (coriander leaves) is reported low at 1 cup in Monash testing, which weighs only about 16 g. Monash also lists fresh herbs among its low FODMAP staples. Dried coriander seed is a separate spice, reported low up to 20 g.

servings.note: No moderate or high amount has been published. The source names no FODMAP group.

notes.text: Dried coriander is reported low up to 20 g in Monash data, with moderate fructose in larger serves.
Monash lists coriander with parsley, thyme, basil and rosemary as fresh herbs that add flavor without FODMAPs.

faq.q: Is cilantro lime rice low FODMAP?
faq.a: The cilantro and rice are fine. Check any added garlic or onion, which many recipes include.

foods.name: basil
foods.answer: Yes. Monash testing reportedly rates 1 cup of fresh basil, about 16 g, as low, and Monash lists fresh and dried herbs among low FODMAP staples. Basil is so light that a cup is a generous handful. Classic pesto is the catch, because of its garlic.

servings.note: No moderate or high amount has been published. The source names no FODMAP group.

notes.text: Monash lists basil in Italian and Indian cooking and Thai basil in Asian cooking as low FODMAP flavorings.

faq.q: Is pesto low FODMAP?
faq.a: Basil is fine, but most pesto has garlic. Make it with garlic-infused oil, and check the nut amount per serve.

foods.name: paprika
foods.answer: Yes, in normal amounts. Monash's reported low serve for paprika is 1 teaspoon (2 g), and larger amounts add fructose. Newer reports say smoked paprika reaches a moderate amount at 5 g. FODMAP Friendly reportedly found no FODMAPs in paprika.

servings.note: Reported Monash low serve. No upper limit was given at the time.

changes.text: George Eats reported that Monash added an upper threshold for regular paprika, with moderate fructose after 7 g.

disagreements.text: Reports on smoked paprika differ: one George Eats page says it is low up to 5 g, another says it is moderate at 5 g.
FODMAP Friendly reportedly lists paprika as free of FODMAPs.

notes.text: Monash lists paprika in Mexican, Moroccan and Spanish cooking as a low FODMAP spice.

faq.q: Is smoked paprika low FODMAP?
faq.a: In small amounts. Reports put its moderate point at about 5 g, so keep the amount per serve modest.

foods.name: cumin
foods.answer: Yes, in normal amounts. A dietitian site reports that Monash tested ground cumin and black cumin seed and rated 2 g portions as low. Monash also lists cumin among spices for low FODMAP cooking. Spice blends are the risk, since many add garlic or onion.

servings.note: Reported Monash low serve. No upper limit has been published. The source names no FODMAP group.

notes.text: Monash names cumin in its Mexican, Indian, Middle Eastern and Moroccan rows of low FODMAP spices.
Monash's shopping list allows most spices, as long as they don't contain garlic or onion.

faq.q: Is whole cumin seed low FODMAP?
faq.a: Black cumin seed (kalonji) was also reported low at 2 g. Regular whole cumin seed is likely similar, but we found no separate public test.

foods.name: garlic powder
foods.answer: Usually not. Garlic powder is dried garlic, and Monash lists it beside fresh garlic as a high-fructan ingredient to look for on labels. Drying removes water, so the fructans are more concentrated by weight. No lab-tested serve is public. Garlic-infused oil is the usual swap.

estimateAnswer.line: Monash lists garlic powder as a high-fructan ingredient. No public lab amount exists.

servings.note: Not lab-tested in public data. Estimated from what it's made of.

notes.text: Fresh garlic is high in fructans even at 3 g, and dried garlic has had its water taken out.
Monash's label guide also flags garlic salt and garlic extract as fructan sources.

faq.q: How much garlic powder is too much?
faq.a: No public lab amount exists. Since fresh garlic is already high at 3 g, assume garlic powder is high in any normal amount.

foods.name: onion powder
foods.answer: Usually not. Onion powder is dried onion, and Monash lists it with onion as a high-fructan ingredient to check for on labels. Drying concentrates the fructans by weight, and no lab-tested serve is public. Spring onion greens, chives or onion-infused oil give onion flavor instead.

estimateAnswer.line: Monash lists onion powder as a high-fructan ingredient. No public lab amount exists.

servings.note: Not lab-tested in public data. Estimated from what it's made of.

notes.text: Many packaged flavors use onion and garlic powder, so it turns up in snacks, stocks and seasonings.
Monash suggests a pinch of asafoetida powder for onion flavor in curries, rice dishes and stews.

faq.q: Is onion salt low FODMAP?
faq.a: No. Monash lists onion salt alongside onion powder as a high-fructan ingredient.

foods.name: chives
foods.answer: Yes. Chives are one of the easiest onion swaps: Monash and FODMAP Friendly both reportedly found no FODMAPs, with a standard serve of 4 g. Dried chives (2 g serve) and Asian or garlic chives (80 g serve) are reported low too.

servings.note: No FODMAPs were reportedly detected, so this is a normal portion, not a limit. The source names no FODMAP group.

disagreements.text: George Eats gives the largest still-low amount instead: up to 500 g per person.

notes.text: Monash's FAQ names chives, with spring onion greens and asafoetida, as ways to add flavor without onion or garlic.

faq.q: Are garlic chives low FODMAP?
faq.a: Yes. Asian (garlic) chives were reported low at an 80 g serve, and they add a mild garlic taste.
